sourceFitAssessment.learnerTask: See why randomization to a whole pre/postoperative sequence cannot isolate its postoperative component.
sourceFitAssessment.gap: The question card is adequate, but the two sequences and differing event clocks would benefit from a compact timeline.
sourceFitAssessment.accuracyGuardrails: Same starting clock and explicitly defined events; pCR patient association is not trial-level surrogacy; do not infer component benefit.
sourceFitAssessment.targetSection: A worked example: a sequence is the tested intervention
sourceFitAssessment.reasoning: One chance assignment begins both whole strategies and both endpoint clocks. Study drug versus placebo appears before and after the same surgery with the same chemotherapy. No second postoperative assignment isolates that component. Alex recurrence while alive and Sam death without prior recurrence correctly distinguish combined recurrence-or-death from death-only endpoints. The pCR association caveat does not assert trial-level surrogacy. The now-committed exact shared phase/purpose/concealment/blinding pair still lacks this whole-sequence and same-origin event comparison, so the pre-art decision remains justified. No dose, schedule, effect size or personal treatment claim is supplied.
